rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating Eve from Adam demonstrates that God can create a living being from another living being, just as He creates from lifeless matter; human generation likewise occurs although Adam could have been created directly from earth.
rows.anchor: إظهار أنه سبحانه قادر على أن يخلق حيا من حي لا على سبيل التوالدكما أنه قادر على أن يخلق حيا من جماد كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged impropriety of Eve's rib-origin is only a groundless intuition: the part's original identity disappeared, and the wisdom of this particular union supports it.
rows.anchor: هذا التشخص الخاص الحاصل لذلك الجزء بحيث لم يبق من تشخصه الأصلي شيء ظاهر يدفع الإستهجان الذي لا مقتضى له إلا الوهم الخالص

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: The Shaykh al-Akbar describes Eve's separation as leaving a void filled by sexual desire: Adam sought its airy occupant, found Eve, and their union began procreation; human union also mirrors the higher cosmic pairing of the First Intellect and Universal Soul.
rows.anchor: فقد ذكر الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره أن حواء لما أنفصلت من آدم عمر موضعها منه بالشهوة النكاحية التي بها وقع الغشيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding discussion suggests this manner of creation was unique to Adam and Eve rather than other animal pairs, but the author has found no fully satisfying evidence on that question.
rows.anchor: ويفهم من كلامهم أن هذا الخلق لم يقع هكذا إلا بين هذين الزوجين دون سائر أزواج الحيوانات ولم أظفر في ذلك بما يشفى الغليل

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that Iblis's wife was created from his left rear rib; al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the relevant term as the shortest ribs of the side.
rows.anchor: نعم أخرج عبد بن حميد وإبن المنذر عن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن زوج إبليس عليهما اللعنة خلقت من خلفه الأيسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse mentions the addressees' creation first because that reminder more directly prompts obedience; fronting “from it” emphasizes Adam as Eve's origin and creates suspense, while “spouse” prepares for reproduction.
rows.anchor: وإنما أخر بيان خلق الزوج عن بيان خلق المخاطبين لما أن تذكير خلقهم أدخل في تحقيق ما هو المقصود

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some critical scholars allow the clause about the spouse to coordinate with an implied clause: God first created the single soul, then created its spouse; the implied clause may stand independently or describe that soul.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى جواز عطف هذه الجملة على مقدر ينبيء عنه السوق لأن تفريع الفروع من أصل واحد يستدعي إنشاء ذلك الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some require the implied clause if the address is universal, to avoid redundancy and the false suggestion that men and women alone were created from both sources; the author considers the objection remote and the added clause unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وأوجب بعضهم هذا التقدير على تقدير جعل الخطاب فيما تقدم عاما في الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He spread from both” means He propagated and dispersed many men and women from the single soul and its spouse through reproduction.
rows.anchor: وبث منهما ( أي نشر وفرق من تلك النفس وزوجها على وجه التناسل والتوالد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “men” and “women” conveys abundance, and “many” modifies “men,” reinforcing that abundance; the author rejects as strained taking it as an adjective for an omitted verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والتلوين في ( رجالا ونساءا ) للتكثير و ( كثيرا ) نعت ل ( رجالا ) مؤكد لما أفاده التنكير والإفراد

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ analyzes “many” as an adjective for an omitted verbal noun, meaning “a great propagation”; the author calls the alternative adjective analysis contrived.
rows.anchor: ونقل أبو البقاء أنه نعت المصدر محذوف أي بثا ( كثيرا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Men and women” means males and females of any age, not only adults; using the gendered terms may intensify the sense of great numbers by portraying each propagated individual as a source of another.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالرجال والنساء البالغين والبالغات بل الذكور والإناث مطلقا تجوزا

rows.speaker: الخطيب
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭīb explains why abundance is stated only for men: wisdom requires women to be more numerous, since a man may have more than one wife whereas a woman cannot have multiple husbands.
rows.anchor: إذ للرجل أن يزيد في عصمته على واحدة بخلاف المرأة قاله الخطيب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer from the verse that every originated thing must arise from prior matter and that creation from absolute nonbeing is impossible; the author rejects this generalization because the verse only identifies the origins of humanity and its mate.
rows.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بالآية على أن الحادث لا يحدث إلا عن مادة سابقة وأن خلق الشيء عن العدم المحض والنفي الصرف محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A case in which matter is used for a particular wise purpose does not establish that all creation requires matter; this verse says only that humans and their mate were created from the stated origins.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لا يلزم من إحداث شيء في صورة واحدة من المادة لحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with “creating” and “spreading” treats the words as coordinated clauses with an omitted subject, since they continue the relative clause; the author contrasts this with coordination of a participle after a finite verb.
rows.anchor: وقريءوخالق وباثعلى حذف المبتدأ لأنه صلة لعطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” repeats and confirms the opening command. The author takes both addresses as directed to the Prophet's original audience; alternatives make both addresses specific to Arabs or the second alone specific to them, but he finds that scope-shift incoherent.
rows.anchor: ( وأتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به ( تكرير للأمر الأول وتأكيد له والمخاطب من بعث إليهم صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا كما مر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to identify the addressees in both commands as Arabs because they habitually invoked one another by God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المخاطب هنا وهناك هم العرب كما روى عن إبن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the majestic name “Allah” instead of a pronoun moves from the attribute of lordship to all attributes of perfection, reinforcing the command to fear Him as creator and deserving of every perfection.
rows.anchor: ووضع الأسم الجليل موضع الضمير للإشارة إلى جميع صفات الكمال ترقيا بعد صفة الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on one another by God in supplication and entreaty itself calls for fearing violation of His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: فإن قول القائل لصاحبه : أسألك بالله وأنشدك الله تعالى على سبيل الإستعطاف يقتضي الإتقاء من مخالفة أوامره ونواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading “you ask one another” can be reciprocal; the form can also carry the meaning “you ask,” since a form with multiple agents may function like the basic verb.
rows.anchor: و ( تساءلون ) إما بمعنى يسأل بعضكم بعضا فالمفاعلة على ظاهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard form originally has two successive tāʾs, one omitted for ease; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and the other Kūfan readers assimilate the first tāʾ into the nearby sīn.
rows.anchor: وأصله على القراءة المشهورة تتساءلونبتاءين فحذفت إحداهما للثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One accusative analysis coordinates “kinship” with the grammatical position of “by Him”; it is supported by the reading “by Him and by kinship,” and reports that people paired kinship with God in pleas, as Mujāhid relates.
rows.anchor: والأرحام بالنصب وهو معطوف إما على محل الجار والمجرور إن كان المحل لهما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reports that people used to couple kinship with God when asking and adjuring one another, saying they asked by God and by the womb/kinship.
rows.anchor: كما أخرج ذلك غير واحد عن مجاهد وهو إختيار الفارسي وعلي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another accusative analysis coordinates “kinship” with the name Allah: fear God and maintain kinship; this is reported from Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās, and ʿIkrima, and preferred by al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj.
rows.anchor: وإما معطوف على الأسم الجليل أي أتقوا الله تعالى والأرحام وصلوها ولا تقطعوها

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī allows the accusative as an exhortation: hold fast to kinship and maintain it.
rows.anchor: وجوز الواحدي النصب على الإغراء أي والزموا الأرحام وصلوها

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads “kinship” in the genitive, conventionally parsed as coordinated with the attached genitive pronoun; most grammarians weaken that construction because the pronoun is tightly bound to its preposition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بالجر وخرجت في المشهور على العطف على الضمير المجرور وضعف ذلك أكثر النحويين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza received this reading through recognized Qurʾān transmitters, was a trusted and learned imam, and was among the seven whose readings leading authorities judged mutawātir; other early authorities also read it, so attacking him is gravely improper.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الإمام أبو حنيفة والثوري ويحيى بن آدم في حقه غلب حمزة الناس على القراءة والفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports that Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and others also read the genitive form.
rows.anchor: بل قرأ به جماعة من غير السبعة كإبن مسعود وإبن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي والحسن البصري وقتادة ومجاهد وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that a genitive attachment cannot follow a preposition-bound pronoun merely reflects Basran grammar; the author rejects binding readers to that school and cites Abū Ḥayyān, the Kūfans, and Ibn Mālik for its grammatical legitimacy in Arabic prose and verse.
rows.anchor: وماذكر من إمتناع العطف على الضمير المجرور هو مذهب البصريين ولسنا متعبدين بإتباعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning kinship does aid the command to fear God: if taqwā means care for human rights, maintaining family ties is among them; if it is general, kinship is included within it.
rows.anchor: لأن التقوى إن أريد بها تقوى خاصة وهي التي في حقوق العباد التي من جملتها صلة الرحم فالتساؤل بالأرحام مما يقتضيه بلا ريب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some answer the objection based on the prohibition of swearing by other than God by limiting that prohibition to oaths made with a belief that fulfillment is obligatory; they cite the report “He prospers, by his father, if truthful.”
rows.anchor: فقد قيل في جوابها : لا نسلم أن الحلف بغير الله تعالى مطلقا منهى عنه بل المنهي عنه ما كان مع إعتقاد وجوب البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish a plea asking another “by kinship” as mere entreaty from swearing “by kinship, I will do it”; they say the former is not covered by the prohibition, and reject the claim that the verse merely reports a pre-Islamic practice.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعضهم أن قول الشخص لآخر : أسألك بالرحم أن تفعل كذا ليس الغرض منه سوى الإستعطاف

rows.speaker: إبن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī offers a further grammatical analysis of Ḥamza's reading based on an omitted element that context makes understood; the next passage develops the proposal.
rows.anchor: وقد خرج إبن جني هذه القراءة على تخريج آخر فقال في الخصائص : باب في أن المحذوف إذا دلت الدلالة عليه كان في حكم الملفوظ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Ibn Jinnī's principle that a contextually evident omission counts as spoken, the author illustrates an omitted “rubb” in a line about a house trace and omitted “bi-khayr” in a greeting; on this analysis Ḥamza's reading omits a preposition already mentioned.
rows.anchor: أي رب رسم دار وكان رؤبو

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also uses omission of the previously mentioned preposition to explain this reading; the author reports al-Kashf's judgment that this is closer for many Basrans because preposition omission is established in comparable expressions.
rows.anchor: وفي شرح المفصل أن الباء في هذه القراءة محذوفة لتقدم ذكرها وقد مشى على ذلك أيضا الزمخشري في أحاجيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the conjunction an oath, as in “Fear God, for by God He watches over me”; omitting the explanatory fāʾ leaves the stronger independent resumption, a good analysis according to the author.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن بعضهم أن الواو للقسم على نحوأتق الله تعالى فوالله إنه مطلع عليكوترك الفاء

rows.speaker: إبن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads “kinship” in the nominative as a subject with an omitted predicate: kinship is likewise to be guarded against severance, or is likewise invoked in mutual requests.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن زيد ( والأرحام ) بالرفع على أنه مبتدأ محذوف الخبر أي ( والأرحام ) كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies “worthy of being maintained” as the omitted predicate, while Ibn Jinnī says “among what you must maintain and protect”; the author finds the clause parenthetical on this reading and the coordination somewhat obscure.
rows.anchor: وقدره إبن عطية أهل لأن توصلو

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said the womb sought refuge from severance after creation, and God promised to join whoever maintains kinship and sever whoever cuts it; al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : إن الله تعالى خلق الخلق حتى إذا فرغ منهم قامت الرحم

rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzār transmits with a good chain a report portraying kinship as clinging to the Throne and praying for connection or severance; God answers that He is the Merciful and reciprocates, since He derived kinship from His name.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البزار بإسناد حسن الرحم حجنة متمسكة بالعرش تكلم بلسان زلق اللهم صل من وصلني

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: A report that Aḥmad transmits with a sound chain calls unjust aggression a form of usury, describes kinship as a branch of the All-Merciful, and says God bars Paradise to whoever severs it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الإمام أحمد بإسناد صحيح إن من أربى الربا الإستطالة بغير حق وإن هذه الرحم شجنة من الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship covers relatives connected by lineage, however distant, and can refer particularly to maternal relatives; restricting the duty of maintaining it to relatives through the mother's womb is unacceptable because commands to treat relatives well are general.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالرحم الأقارب ويقع على كل من يجمع بينك وبينه نسب وإن بعد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains “watchful over you” as “preserving you”; al-Rāghib derives the expression from watching in the sense of guarding.
rows.anchor: إن الله كان عليكم رقيبا 1 أي حفيظا قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: إبن زيد
rows.claim: The word may also mean one who observes or knows: Ibn Zayd interprets it as “knowing,” by analogy with a high lookout from which a place is observed; grammatically it is an active participle.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا فسره إبن زيد بالعالم وعلى كل فهو فعيل بمعنى فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause explains why the command and compliance are obligatory; naming God explicitly reinforces that rationale, and fronting the prepositional phrase maintains the verse's rhyme.
rows.anchor: والجملة في موضع التعليل للأمر ووجوب الإمتثال وإظهار الأسم الجليل لتأكيده وتقديم الجار لرعاية الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited women are prohibited as objects of marriage, not as persons: legal prohibition concerns acts, marriage is the salient intended act, and the surrounding context concerns marriage; therefore the verse is not ambiguous, contrary to al-Karkhī.
rows.anchor: والمراد تحريم نكاحهن لأنه معظم ما يقصد منهن ولأنه المتبادر إلى الفهم ولأن ما قبله وما بعده في النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author regards the clause as performative rather than a report of a past prohibition; some investigators allow a report-like reading, taking the past form as timeless as in formal definitions.
rows.anchor: والجملة إنشائية وليس المقصود منها الإخبار عن التحريم في الزمان الماضي وقال بعض المحققين : لا مانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form is used because it is obvious that God is the one who made these women forbidden.
rows.anchor: وبني الفعل لما لم يسم فاعله لأنه لا يشتبه أن المحرم هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your mothers” includes grandmothers at every level because “mother” denotes an origin, as in “Mother of the Book” and “Mother of Cities”; on this analysis the term's true sense includes them.
rows.anchor: و ( أمهاتكم ) تعم الجدات كيف كن إذ الأم هي الأصل في الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some treat “mother” for a grandmother as figurative and establish the prohibition by consensus; the author says the intended meaning is “origin” either way, so grandmothers fall under the general figurative usage, with consensus identifying that intent.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن إطلاق الأم على الجدة مجاز وأن إثبات حرمة الجدات بالإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daughters include one's own daughter and descendants' daughters: “daughter” can truly mean a branch, or may be extended to descendants figuratively; even those who deny that extension accept their prohibition by consensus.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالبنات من ولدتها أو ولدت من ولدها وتسمية الثانية بنتا حقيقة بإعتبار أن البنت يراد به الفرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of grandmothers and descendants' daughters can also follow from the text's indication: aunts are daughters of grandmothers, and descendants' daughters are closer than nieces, so the nearer relations are prohibited a fortiori.
rows.anchor: قد يستدل على تحريم الجدات وبنات الأولاد بدلالة النص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent Arabic meaning prohibits marrying one's biological daughter born of fornication, since no evidence transfers the ordinary meaning of “daughter” to a technical legal meaning here.
rows.anchor: ثم ظاهر النص يدل على أنه يحرم للرجل بنته من الزنا لأنها بنته والخطاب إنما هو باللغة العربية مالم يثبت نقل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits the fornication-born daughter to her biological father because lineage and its other legal consequences are not established for her, citing the Prophetic dictum that a child belongs to the marital bed.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك خلاف الإمام الشافعي رضي ا لله تعالى عنه فقد قال : إن المخلوقة من ماء الزنا تحل للزاني

rows.speaker: بعض الشافعية
rows.claim: Some Shāfiʿīs say the daughter becomes forbidden if the Prophet Jesus, at his descent, informs the man that she was conceived from his semen; the author replies that the Lawgiver severed her lineage from him, so her physical origin is irrelevant.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الشافعية : تحرم إن أخبره نبيكعيس عليه السلاموقت نزوله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Opponents of the prohibition argue that biological paternity cannot suffice: a man who buys a virgin, deflowers her, and later fathers a child is not automatically assigned that child without acknowledgment; legal lineage cannot suffice either, since Muslim consensus denies the fornication-born child lineage from the fornicator.
rows.anchor: وأعترضوا على القائلين بالحرمة بأنهم إما أن يثبتوا كونها بنتا له بناءا على الحقيقة لكونها مخلوقة من مائه أو بناءا على حكم الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that biological fact makes a person the daughter of the man whose semen produced her, whether licitly or illicitly; physical part-wholeness is the basis of the marriage prohibition, and the mother is certainly forbidden her own child born of fornication.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بإختيار الشق الأول إذ لا خلاف بين أهل اللسان في أن المخلوقة من ماء إنسان بنته سواء كان ذلك الماء ماء حلال أو سفاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between a child separating bodily from its mother and a daughter separating from her father only mentally does not disprove shared substance; Arabic calls a child a piece of its father, and absence of inheritance from the father is due to consensus, not lack of true daughterhood.
rows.anchor: والتفرقة بين المسألتين بأن الولد في المسألة الثانية بعضها وأنفصل منها إنسانا ولا كذلك البنت في المسألة الأولى لأنها أنفصلت منه ذهنيا لا تفيد سوى أن البعضية في المسألة الثانية أظهر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: In the school discussion of a concubine's child, Abū Ḥanīfa says that if the master did not withdraw and protected her from suspicion, religious duty obliges him to claim the child; withdrawal or failure to protect her creates a contrary presumption allowing denial.
rows.anchor: فالمروى عن أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنهأنه إن كان حين وطئها لم يعزل عنها

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abū Yūsuf says a master must claim a child born before he performed post-intercourse waiting, whether or not he withdrew or protected the woman, out of good opinion of her; this matches the majority.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي يوسف إذا وطئها ولم يستبرئها بعد ذلك حتى جاءت بولد فعليه ان يدعيه سواء عزل عنها أو لم يعزل حصنها أو لم يحصنها تحسينا للظن بها

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Muḥammad says the master should not claim the child if he does not know it is his, but should free the child; al-Īḍāḥ presents both Abū Yūsuf's claim and Muḥammad's emancipation as recommendations.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد لا ينبغي أن يدعي ولدها إذا لم يعلم أنه منه ولكن ينبغي أن يعتق الولد

rows.speaker: بعض فضلاء الدرس
rows.claim: A scholar in the lesson argues that admission of intercourse aimed at procreation, or admission that the master did not withdraw and protected the woman, should establish lineage without requiring a separate statement “this is my son”; the author sees no obstacle to adopting this position in the school.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا قال بعض فضلاء الدرس : ينبغي أنه لو أقر أنه كان لا يعزل عنها وحصنها أن يثبت نسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mabsūṭ says that a long delay supports assigning the child to the master because his conduct, such as accepting congratulations, indicates acknowledgment and functions like an explicit admission.
rows.anchor: وفي المبسوط أنه إذا تطاول الزمان ألحق به لأن التطاول دليل إقراره لأنه يوجد منه حينئذ ما يدل على الإقرار من قبول التهنئة ونحوه
